Interesting! When `_farkas_ok` is forced to always return False, the fallback (capped minimization) also fails because it uses the same `_farkas_ok` check. That's expected behavior for this artificial test — the fallback path itself works but the check rejects it. My test was flawed: forcing `_farkas_ok` to False breaks both paths.

Let me instead test the capped-minimization fallback by making only the *first* Farkas LP result rejected. I'll patch `_linprog` inside `_farkas`... simpler: monkeypatch `_farkas_ok` with a counter that returns False only on the first call per Farkas invocation. Let me do that.

Also note the first two modes printed nothing in the tail — let me see the full output to confirm modes 1 and 2 passed.
